transcript.text: Had a new induction hob fitted by a mate last month. Tonight the big red cooker switch on the wall was hot to touch, there's a burning plastic smell and the hob keeps cutting out. What's going on?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning smell or smoke can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Stop using the hob and isolate it at the wall switch (fused spur) immediately. A hot cooker switch combined with a burning plastic smell is a serious safety hazard indicating an overheating electrical connection, likely due to loose wiring from the recent installation or a fault drawing excessive current. Do not try to fix this yourself or reset the switch repeatedly, as this poses a fire risk. You need a qualified electrician to inspect the fused spur and the hob's hard-wiring connections to find and repair the loose or damaged connection.

candidates.cause: Loose or overheating connection at the fused spur (cooker switch)
Earth leakage fault in hob power module causing high current draw
